analysis:
Documentation-only changes in docs/architecture/inference.md. The base lines 810-811 and 827 described GLM5Next video decoding as refusing variable-frame-rate (VFR) tracks with a deterministic 400. The head text (lines 810-813, 829) now says VFR tracks are indexed at i / nominalFrameRate, as in the reference loader. Head lines 1896-1899 add inline video data-URI labels (mp4, x-m4v, quicktime, mov) gated by MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders; that excerpt is truncated.

Security relevance: accepting VFR widens the decoder input surface for adversarial consumers (ADV-002) under TB-007. The documented bounds are unchanged: the 512 MiB maximumDecodedBytes decoded-frame cap, the 28,532 prepared-pixel token cap, the VisionMemoryGate reservation, maxVideoDurationSeconds 600 and the per-request media limits. Media remains excluded from prefix lookup and capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041 exposure is unchanged.

Integration question: confirm that the GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset source enforces the frame-count/decoded-byte cap independently of nominalFrameRate. A zero, NaN or extremely low or high nominalFrameRate could otherwise distort the sampled-frame or timestamp computation, or cause excessive frame reads or a division fault. The source code was not supplied, so this is a coverage limit, not a finding.

Also confirm that the new MIME labels only gate parsing and that the container is still validated by AVFoundation decode. No threat-model asset, boundary or mitigation is invalidated by the documentation text alone.
